content: pull_request_target and similar triggers run workflows in the base repo's privileged context (secrets + write GITHUB_TOKEN) even when checking out a fork's code; if that checked-out code executes on a self-hosted runner, an attacker gets immediate high-privilege access to whatever the runner can reach. Self-hosted runners should generally never be used for public repos or workflows triggerable by external contributors' PRs without required-approval gating; avoid pull_request_target unless absolutely necessary, and never execute forked PR code with secrets available.
